text:
Like motionless beasts stretched upon the sand,
they turn their eyes toward the ocean horizon,
and their seeking feet and joined hands
have sweet faintings and bitter tremors.

Some, hearts that love confidences,
deep in the wood where the stream sings,
spell out the love of their timid puberty
and mark the tender trees upon the trunk;

Others, like sisters, walk grave and slow
through rocks filled with apparitions,
where Saint Anthony saw surge like lava
those temptations with naked breasts;

And there are some who, by the light of dripping resins,
in the now mute hollows of pagan caves,
call upon you to aid their howling fever,
O Bacchus, who lulls every anxiety!

And others, whose throats display scapulars,
who hide a whip beneath their long robes,
mingle, in lonely nights and shadowy groves,
the foam of pleasure with the tears of torture.

O virgins, O monsters, O demons, O martyrs,
spirits disdainful of all reality,
craving infinity, devout women, satyrs,
now taut with screams, now dissolved in tears,

You whom my soul pursued into such hell,
my sisters, I love and pity you
for your muffled sorrows, your insatiable thirst,
and the urns of love your breasts contain.

translation.title: Damned Women
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The poem’s address to women marked by desire, devotion, punishment, and social condemnation is retained.
